notes: The wrong-answer explanation writes the variable as a bare lowercase l ("So l + w = P ÷ 2 = 9"), which in this font is a plain vertical stroke sitting right next to digits and reads as "1 + w". Spell it out as "length + width" or use L.

The prompt is clipped in both modes — the card cuts off after "How many unit cubes", losing "does it contain?"; in keypad mode the fourth line is sliced through mid-glyph. Separately the Box3D labels are ~8px and only two of the three edges are labelled (5 and 5, with the 4 left to be counted).

The prompt is clipped in both modes — MC ends at "The second is 2 × 4 × 3 cubic" and drops "units. What is the total volume?", keypad slices a line in half. The diagram is also a single plain unlabelled cube, which does not depict the two-prism composite figure the prompt describes.

The edge-length label "4" is ~10px (half the size of any other text) and is printed inside the centre face of the net rather than alongside an edge, so it reads as a label for that face rather than as the cube's edge length.

The ⁴⁄₃ in the explanation renders as superscript/subscript glyphs about half the height of the surrounding text — the smallest thing on the screen — and is inconsistent with the precomposed ⅓ used one concept over in volume_cone.
The wrong-answer explanation only restates the answer ("This shape is a square.") with no defining property, so a kid who picked triangle learns nothing about why.
Same as identify_shape_2d: the explanation is just "This 3D shape is a cube." with no distinguishing feature to separate it from the sphere/cylinder/cone distractors.
